title: thief: deadly shadows
text: This is the 3rd game in the thief franchise, following Garrett exploits who always for some reason unwillingly getting himself involved in some world ending event that he accidently help to start and now must stop it. I have played the previous thief games in the series and I have entered this game with low expectations since I heard that this game is not a proper/good thief game and that this game is a step backward but I got to tell you that this game actually a very good and a proper thief game. Yes, it's flawed and feel rushed but it's still a good game. The graphics are very beautiful and aged very well and although I personally prefer the artstyle of thief 1 and 2 cutscenes, the cutscenes of this game have their own charm which I approve. Lockpicking is now a minigame....finally, you can climb down ladders safely without falling to your death now, new interesting gear to use like the gas bombs and the oil and the most important thing - you got a loot tracker where you can see how much loot you got in the middle of mission and how much still left around waiting for you to steal it. There are very serious problem and flaws with this game and I feel that they are as a result of a rushed release: The way Garrett move in this game is very sluggish compare to how he moved in the previous games, it feels like he moves in molasses,  and for some reason you can get stuck on the terrain and in some instances you will start to skate on the floor because it appears that you got stuck on the falling animation. The concept of the city is cool, you can go to other people houses, some stores and pubs and steal their stuff. There are also handlers that you can visit sell them your ill-gotten loot and blackmarket shops that will sell you equipment for your next missions and items for your house (this is instead of the starting menu before each mission in the previous game)...but again it feels like it was rushed and poorly implemented. The problem with the city is not the thing that I mentioned before, no, those work as they were intended.... it’s the city guards....not the other hostile NPC in the area......it’s the annoying stupid city guards. It becomes tiresome to evade every time those guards in order to get from one section of the city to the other, these guys are everywhere, and it becomes more of a nuisance then a challenge as you continue to play. I get the factions that can be hostile to you, but those have their special areas where you know you want to stay away from there unless you need something specific there…but the guards, there are just too many of them for the sizes of each quarter. I get it if the city would have shortcuts and more hidden routes to get around the guard problem but there aren't any. The difficulty adjustment is not well implemented, for example in the original thief games you were forbidden to kill anyone(because a true master thief don’t need to kill) but here on expert you are allowed to do so. Also to those who did the mission with the captain's widow: on that mission you need to get 90% of the loot on expert and you reach a point in the game were it is told that the widow will need the money in the specific chest to survive which is worth 12% of the total loot in the mission and you can see the problem…so on the other difficulties I would not have taken it...but apparently the devs didn’t playtest this part at the time and rushed it out. Other than that I have really enjoyed the game; the funny dialogues are still there…though I miss the Hammerites funny voice acting. Each mission feels different, especially the Shalebridge Cradle one, and the main villain and its minions are very unnerving. Final words? it's not a perfect thief game but still a good one. BTW this game is old and need patching with some fan made patches in order to played on modern systems without any problems. Go to the PCGAMINGWIKI site for the essential improvements and install the latest version of the Sneaky Upgrade patch in order to make the game more stable, add widescreen and choose what mods to install (or you can leave it vanilla).

title: thinking with time machine
text: Probably the closest we'll get to Portal 3. Overall, a wonderfully satisfying mod. Weak points of this mod: - The story is very thin. Don't expect the carefully-planned plot of Portal 1 or 2. It sets the premise but that's about it. It's almost entirely superfluous. The ending is almost nonsensical, but in the end, it's about as sensible as the rest of what passes for a plot. Fortunately, the point of this mod isn't the story. - It is also quite short. Expect about 1 hour play time. That's understandable, considering the small number of people who made this. But I really enjoyed it, so 9 levels aren't enough! - The progression of difficulty is a bit out-of-order. The hardest level was about half-way through (level 6, I think), and thereafter things seemed to get easier. But maybe that was just my learning curve. Strong points of this mod: - This mod is well made, especially considering the small number of people behind it. The visual style is very nice--it is unique to the mod, but based heavily on Portal 2's graphics, so you still feel that you're in a different section of the same game. Everything is so shiny and smooth! The sound clips and so on are pretty much all from Portal 2 as well. I had no problem with glitchy graphics. - The time machine mechanism is explained nicely with computer screens that have Bendy demonstrating various skills. Much like the original Portal, the first several chambers are very helpful in building up your skills for the harder levels later on. This is a very useful way of teaching how to use the time machine without changing the feel of Portal too much, because, unlike cube- and button-based testing, it's not at all obvious from the get-go. - The actual mechanism of the time machine is *very* fun. I feel that it wasn't utilised to its full extent here--there is a lot more that could be done with it. But most of the chambers have multiple solutions, all requiring use of the time machine, so you can play to your strengths and figure things out in a variety of ways. - Level design is very nice. As in Portal, the early levels make it fairly clear what needs solving, but later ones become more open-ended. Every level has been designed with the time machine strongly in mind. It's quite impressive, when you consider the potential complexity given by the time machine. - It's free! Considering the price ($0), this is definitely worth playing. I would absolutely recommend it as a fun mini-continuation of Portal 2. The graphics, mechanism, and level design are all at a very high standard, higher than most games that cost actual money.

title: this war of mine
text: This war of mine is a dark story of war, morals, and survival. This game is centered around keeping the characters in your control alive. It may seem like any other survival game, another dont starve remix but no. When playing this game one factor sets it apart from the rest of the survival games out there, you cannot go and colect supplied during the day. You get a small amount of loot in your safehouse when you start but after thats depleted you have to scavenge for supplies during the night. And when you go scavenging you only have a small inventory to carry things in. This makes your rescorces feel much more scarce. The gameplay boils down to two timeframes: Night and day. During the day you have to stay indoors due to snipers and other dangers. During this time you have to craft things you have found in you shelter or that you have scavenged. you also must keep your group fed and satiate there other needs. During the night time you can assign members of your group to sleep, guard the safehouse or scavenge in certain locations. You start out with only three members so you must take into account how much they can carry certain stats associated with them and there needs to decide these things. The various locations you can loot are scripted and show up at certain times, Meaning you cannot go everywhere from the beginning. The game establishes a feeling of desperation that rivals day z as your group members can get sick, wounded etc. Whats nice and helps to establish the theme of desperation is that if your members get sick you cannot ignore it until it goes away. you must give them medicine or bandages and let them rest for awhile until they get better. If you ignore a certain condition it could get worse and will resault in a certain charcter becauming less useful.

text: A very unique experience that I highly recommend everyone tries, even if you don't like the survival genre as I myself don't and I still enjoyed This War of Mine quite a lot. I don't feel like the game has much replayability in the sense that you don't want to keep playing it because it can get quite tedious due to the lack of any sort of fast forwarding, and once you've found the best "build" you are basically replaying the same campaign over and over just making slight tweaks depending on your spawning circumstances which does get boring. Once I had successfully survived until the end of the war once and explored all the buildings I feel like I had seen everything the game had to offer and I was done. In the end I got 14 hours of enjoyment out of the game for £3.74 and it genuinely moved me at times, which is very rare for a game to do. It's also beautifully designed, the art style really does add to the desperation you feel as the days turn into weeks and you're on the brink of death, just looking for a scrap of food to make it to the next day alive. 7/10

text: This really is a unique game. The subtly awesome soundtrack fused with the brilliant voice acting by Danny Wallace actually makes you really care about the rectangular protagonists. Each character has his own faults which mirrors the real world and has in game consequences. The slow, tiny cube that can't bear the fact that another jolly cube is helping him out. The giant rectangular who makes it his job to help out the little people. The end ties everything together and is really touching. The puzzle elements of the game are very well made and, while I don't play many puzzle platformers, i didn't find it toooo tricky making my way through the game. A really nice timeout from all my other fast-paced games.

text: This game is defiently my favorite game of all time. Each level gets harder and harder, and you meet new friends along the way. You start off as Thomas (Just a simple red rectangle) and defeat jumping puzzles and basically, just jump around. Finishing the game is a big achievement, it took me about a week (8.5hrs) to finish this game The graphics are outstounding, and it runs perfectly. Don't worry if you think you computer can't handle the graphics (Even my computer is crappy, and I had it ran perfectly on the best graphics) you can change them once you start the game up. I love the music in the backround, and the narrator talking at the start of each level helps a lot. If you feel like you have done something wrong in a level and don't know how to fix it, don't worry, you can just hit "Esc" on your keyboard and then click "Restart" on the side of the screen with the cursor. I think this game is for everyone and everything, you should really try it. This game is well worth your money. I rate this magnificent game a 9.5 out of 10.

title: thomas was alone
text: As a puzzle platformer, this is a very competent, not-too-challenging game. Where Thomas Was Alone knocks it out of the park is with the mass amounts of heart and soul behind the game. If you would have told me a week ago that not only would a game make me care deeply about monochromatic digital quadrilaterals, but also that said quadrilaterals would comprise one of the most enduring, memorable casts of any game this generation, I would have laughed in your face. But Thomas Was Alone pulls this off with a pitch perfect combination of excellent writing, a moody ambient soundscape, beautiful art, and a narrator that pulls everything together in a way that I've only seen rivaled in Bastion. Thomas Was Alone is one of the most charming games I've played, and is not only full of heart, but is extremely fun as well. This is a great game.

title: thomas was alone
text: Thomas Was Alone is a very good game. The storyline is quite good, the characters are very well developed, and the gameplay is really well done. The storyline of Thomas Was Alone is about . The storyline is not just encompassing the situation, but also the characters. Along with the storyline, the character design comes along. The character design is quite good, each character is a rectangle or a square, each of varying sizes, this is how the is repersented. The game itself is not too long, but doesn't feel too short either. The character development is really good in this game, as each individual character have thought processes, and each character has their own little insecurities, hopes, dreams, and interests. This is contrasted beautifully with the minimalist character desgin in the game. The game includes female characters as well are male characters, and they are both written equally in depth. Each character has a name, which should not be odd for games, but the addition of names really does help to build the character's personality, making them less of just shapes and more of actual characters. Despite what the title says, there is no real protagonist (at least not from what I could see), each character was as important as the last, and probably appeared just as often as each other. As in this game each character has a special ability, it becomes impossible to create favourites, as they all are very useful and have their own traits. This game is a puzzle/platformer game. You need to solve the puzzle of getting all of the characters to their little glowing boxes (which reinforces the idea that all the characters are equally worthy), this is often done by using the special ability of each of the characters to your advantage, this makes the game less of a puzzle game, and more of a teamwork game. Despite the changing between characters being slightly tedious, the overall gameplay is quite smooth. There are no levels that I got stuck on that made me dread continuing the game, quite the contrary, I felt compelled to continue to play more and more, to the point I had to limit my sessions. Along with the gameplay, the achievements in the game are quite nice, they provide more replayability, and revisiting of levels, and are not too hard to achieve, but not stupidly easy. Thomas Was Alone is quite a good game, it's not too long. The game has brilliant character development, and the gameplay can be tedious, but is quite natural. I would recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a nice game to get them thinking, but also to calm down and enjoy a really good story.

title: time clickers
text: This is my 4th Clicker game, and it really is the first of the 2nd generation of Clicker games! Targeted Clicker game! You have to aim at different bricks, you cant just click anymore, you also have to hit them.... thats why you use guns in this game. Sounds like a small thing, but really chances the whole game, great thing! Also nice graphics! Also, there are some decisions differnt to other Clicker games; The Time Cubes you earn, in contrast to other clicker games, always count towards DPS once activated... even if you use them for upgrading of skills... this makes every run count... as you at least get stronger! Makes the mid to end game a bit easier to grind through... The concept of differently colored blocks, which are worth different amounts of gold is also very clever! Soon, there will be IDLE mode (currently you only gain very little money, but you dont progress in levels)... NIce achievements give you a reason to get going and continue. And most importantly, its really F2P.. there is no store, you cant buy anything... just beat the game fair! 9/10.

title: time clickers
text: So much more fun than clicker heroes. Don't have to spend hours on the reddit or wiki trying to figure out how to get anywhere. No horribly complicated calculations. The time cubes (Hero Souls in CH) act like talent points in rpgs but you never lose the DPS bonus when you buy the talents. This means you are always getting stronger. You can never make yourself weaker by spending points early. I am sure there is a optimum path to upgrade through, but it does not matter that much compared to Clicker Heroes. Oh just a tip. For your first several runs, time warp as soon as you can. Level 100 gets you 10 time cubes. Levels 105, 110, 115, 120 get you you 3-4 time cubes. But getting to past 110 takes a little while at first.

title: time clickers
text: An adequate clicker game with sharp graphics and pretty decent music. I do like the way that achievements are handled in the game and the idea of different "sub level" upgrades to your clicker tools is pretty neat. You can upgrade to a level that increases speed, or damage, or has some other function like targetting random blocks. Otherwise as the levels climb into the thousands, the sharpness of the grind goes up pretty fast. Not as much as some other games, and the changing scenery is nice, but it does get repetitive. After restarting and spending time cubes and weapons cubes on various upgrades and new abilities, there's only so many ways to keep things fresh. Overall entertaining, but not something to keep attention more than a couple weeks.
